topics.title: Meaning and Essentials of Contingent Contracts
explain: An absolute contract is performed unconditionally, whereas a contingent contract depends on a future uncertain event.
Section 31 defines a contingent contract as one to do or not to do something if some event, collateral to such contract, does or does not happen.
Contracts of insurance, indemnity, and guarantee are classic examples of contingent contracts.
A collateral event is neither direct performance promised nor the whole consideration, but connected to the contract (Pollock and Mulla).
The contingent event must be uncertain and must not depend solely on the mere arbitrary will of the promisor.

flow.title: Checking if a Contract is Contingent
steps: Contract performance depends on an event
Event is collateral to main promise
Event is future and uncertain
Event is not purely promisor's will
Contract is classified as contingent

topics.example: A contracts to pay B ₹10,00,000 if B's house is burnt. This is a valid contingent contract because burning of the house is a collateral uncertain event.
remember: Insurance, indemnity, and guarantee contracts fall under contingent contracts.
mistakes: Confusing a conditional contract (like delivering wheat and paying afterwards) with a contingent contract where the event is collateral.

quiz.q: Which section of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 defines a 'Contingent Contract'?
quiz.why: Section 31 specifically defines a contingent contract.

quiz.q: A promises to pay B ₹50,00,000 to buy B's house if A is able to secure a bank loan. What type of contract is this?
quiz.why: The performance depends on securing a bank loan, which is a collateral uncertain event.

topics.title: Rules Relating to Enforcement of Contingent Contracts
explain: Sec 32: Contracts contingent on an event happening can only be enforced when that event happens; if the event becomes impossible, it becomes void.
Sec 33: Contracts contingent on an event NOT happening are enforceable when that event becomes impossible or fails to happen.
Sec 34: If contingent on a living person's conduct, it becomes impossible if that person acts in a way preventing the event (Frost v. Knight).
Sec 35: Contracts contingent on happening or non-happening of a specified event within a fixed time become void or enforceable based on time expiry.
Sec 36: Agreements contingent on an impossible event are void ab initio, whether the impossibility is known or unknown to the parties.

flow.title: Enforcement Logic for Contingent Contracts
steps: Identify the future contingent event
Check if event is happening or non-happening
Verify if fixed time applies
Determine if event occurred or became impossible
Enforce contract or declare it void

topics.example: A promises to pay B a sum of money when B marries C. If C dies without marrying B, the contract becomes void under Section 32.
remember: Sections 32 to 36 govern enforcement rules for contingent contracts.
Agreements contingent on impossible events (Sec 36) are void ab initio.
Frost v. Knight illustrates impossibility created by a living person's conduct (Sec 34).
mistakes: Thinking a contract contingent on an impossible event becomes void only when discovered; it is void ab initio from the very beginning.

quiz.q: What is the legal status of an agreement contingent on an impossible event under Section 36?
quiz.why: Section 36 clearly states that contingent agreements on impossible events are void ab initio.

quiz.q: In Frost v. Knight, why was the defendant held liable for breach of contract under Section 34 principles?
o: The father died before the marriage
He married another woman during father's lifetime
The plaintiff refused to marry him
The fixed period of one year expired
quiz.why: By marrying another woman, the defendant rendered it impossible to marry the plaintiff.

topics.title: Distinction Between Contingent Contract and Wagering Contract
explain: A contingent contract is valid in law, whereas a wagering agreement is void.
In a contingent contract, the event is collateral; in a wager, the uncertain event is the core factor determining money transfer.
Wagering agreements consist of reciprocal promises, while contingent contracts may not contain reciprocal promises.
Parties in a contingent contract have a real interest in the subject matter, whereas wagering parties only care about winning or losing money.
Wagering contracts are based on mutuality of gain and loss, which is absent in contingent contracts.

flow.title: Distinguishing Contingent from Wagering Contracts
steps: Check party interest in subject matter
Check presence of reciprocal promises
Check if event is collateral or core
If core with sole interest, it is Wagering
If valid interest with collateral event, it is Contingent

topics.example: An insurance policy on a house is a valid contingent contract because the owner has a real insurable interest in the house.
remember: Contingent contracts are valid; Wagering agreements are void.
Parties to a contingent contract have an insurable/real interest in the subject matter.
mistakes: Assuming all contracts that depend on uncertain future events are wagering contracts.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a key characteristic of a wagering contract compared to a contingent contract?
o: The contracting parties have genuine insurable interest
It consists of reciprocal promises and is void
The event is collateral to the contract
quiz.why: Wagering contracts consist of reciprocal promises and are void in law.

quiz.q: What is the legal status of a contract of insurance?
quiz.why: Insurance is a valid contingent contract because the insured party has a real interest in the subject matter.

topics.title: Meaning and Salient Features of Quasi Contracts
explain: Quasi contracts are obligations created by law without a formal agreement, offer, acceptance, or consensus ad idem.
They are based on principles of equity, justice, good conscience, and preventing unjust enrichment.
The fundamental maxim is: 'No man must grow rich out of another person's loss'.
A quasi-contractual right is always a right to money, generally a liquidated sum of money.
It is a right in personam, meaning it is available against a specific person or persons, not against the whole world.

flow.title: How Law Imposes a Quasi Contract
steps: No formal contract or agreement exists
One party gets a benefit or enrichment
Enrichment would be unjust at other's loss
Law creates an obligation to pay or restore
Enforced like a regular contract

topics.example: T, a tradesman, leaves goods at C's house by mistake. C treats the goods as his own and consumes them. C is bound by law to pay T.
remember: Quasi-contracts prevent unjust enrichment ('No man must grow rich out of another person's loss').
Rights under quasi-contracts are rights in personam to money.
mistakes: Thinking quasi-contracts require mutual agreement; they are strictly imposed by law without consent.

quiz.q: Quasi-contracts are based on which equitable doctrine?
quiz.why: Quasi-contracts prevent a person from unjustly enriching themselves at another person's expense.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a salient feature of a quasi-contract?
o: It creates a right in rem against the whole world
It is a right to money against a specific person imposed by law
It requires express offer and acceptance
quiz.why: Quasi-contracts create a right in personam for money imposed by law.

topics.title: Cases Deemed as Quasi-Contracts
explain: Sec 68: Claim for necessaries supplied to an incompetent person (minor/lunatic) is recoverable from their property, not personally.
Sec 69: Payment by an interested person: a person paying money another is legally bound to pay is entitled to reimbursement.
Sec 70: Obligation of person enjoying benefits of a non-gratuitous act to pay compensation or restore the thing (Shyam Lal v. State of U.P.).
Sec 71: Finder of lost goods has duties of a bailee: care for property, no right to appropriate, return to true owner (Hollins v. Howler).
Sec 72: Money paid or goods delivered by mistake or coercion must be repaid/returned (Shivprasad v. Sirish Chandra; Sales Tax Officer v. Kanhaiyalal; Trikamdas v. BMC).

flow.title: Identifying Deemed Quasi-Contract Cases
steps: Check situation under Sections 68 to 72
Sec 68: Necessaries to incompetent person
Sec 69: Payment by interested party
Sec 70: Benefit of non-gratuitous act taken
Sec 71: Finder of lost goods
Sec 72: Payment by mistake or coercion
Law enforces obligation to compensate or return

topics.example: A delivers a fruit parcel by mistake to R, who eats it thinking it's a gift. R must pay A for the fruits under Section 70.
remember: Section 68: Reimbursed from minor's/lunatic's property only (no personal liability).
Section 69: Interested person paying another's legal liability.
Section 72: Payment by mistake or coercion.
mistakes: Holding a minor personally liable under Sec 68 instead of limiting recovery strictly to the minor's property.

quiz.q: Under Section 68, how can a person who supplies necessaries to a minor recover the amount?
o: Only from the property of the minor
From the minor's legal guardian personally
quiz.why: Section 68 allows reimbursement only from the property of the incompetent person.

quiz.q: What is the legal status and responsibility of a finder of lost goods under Section 71?
o: Absolute owner against everyone including true owner
quiz.why: Section 71 provides that a finder of lost goods is subject to the same responsibility as a bailee.

topics.title: Distinction Between Quasi Contracts and Contracts
explain: In a valid contract, essential elements like offer, acceptance, consideration, and free consent are present.
In a quasi-contract, all essential elements for contract formation are completely absent.
Contracts are created by the voluntary consent and agreement of the contracting parties.
Quasi-contracts are not created by consent; obligations are imposed strictly by operation of law.
Contracts create rights based on promises, whereas quasi-contracts create legal duties to prevent unjust enrichment.

flow.title: Comparing Contract vs Quasi-Contract Creation
steps: Is there an offer and acceptance?
If YES: Consent forms a Contract
If NO: Check if law imposes obligation
Law imposes duty to prevent unjust enrichment
It is classified as a Quasi Contract

topics.example: Ordering food at a restaurant creates a regular contract by consent. Receiving wrong food delivery and consuming it creates a quasi-contract obligation by law.
remember: Quasi Contracts = Imposed by law without agreement.
mistakes: Assuming quasi-contracts are actual contracts; they are non-contractual legal duties enforced as if they were contracts.

quiz.q: What is the primary source of obligation in a quasi-contract?
quiz.why: Quasi-contractual obligations are strictly imposed by law, not by party consent.

quiz.q: Are the essential elements of a valid contract (such as offer and acceptance) present in a quasi-contract?
quiz.why: The essential elements for the formation of a valid contract are absent in quasi-contracts.
